item.title: 🇷🇺 On November 13, Russia’s Deputy Foreign Minister Sergey Ryabkov and Cuba’s First Deputy Foreign Minister
item.description: 🇷🇺 🇨🇺 📞 On November 13, Russia’s Deputy Foreign Minister Sergey Ryabkov and Cuba’s First Deputy Foreign Minister Gerardo Penalver had a telephone conversation at the Cuban Side’s initiative. They discussed current bilateral cooperation issues . Sergey Ryabkov reaffirmed Russia’s principled position that economic and military pressure on Cuba is unacceptable and that the US trade, fuel and financial blockade of the island must end immediately . 🤝 He expressed unwavering solidarity with and support for the leadership and people of the fraternal country in these difficult times, and reiterated Russia’s readiness to continue providing Havana with the necessary political and material assistance. #RussiaCuba

🎙
Russia’s Deputy Foreign Minister Dmitry Lyubinsky
answer to a media question
from
TASS news agency
on the Nord Stream gas pipelines
(November 13, 2026)
❓
Question: In October, the Higher Regional Court in Hamburg, Germany, began hearing the case concerning the bombing of the Nord Stream gas pipelines. Several hearings have now taken place. How does Russia view the trial and its coverage in the Western media?
💬
Dmitry Lyubinsky:
We are following the trial in Hamburg of Ukrainian national
Sergey Kuznetsov
, who is accused of
blowing up
the Nord Stream 1 and Nord Stream 2 gas pipelines in 2022. The proceedings began in October 2026 and are due to conclude in June 2027.
We would like to believe that this trial will not turn into yet another farce
, as the national investigations in Germany, Denmark and Sweden did.
On various pretexts, the authorities in those countries
avoided cooperating with Russian law enforcement agencies
on the case
, disregarding, among other things, their obligations under international conventions on counter-terrorism.
Stories have been deliberately planted in the Western media, and the practice continues.
The aim is to ensure that those who organised, commissioned and oversaw this act of sabotage, which the German judiciary has classified as a war crime, escape identification and punishment.
The Financial Times
recently weighed in, reporting that it was
indeed Kuznetsov
who carried out the bombings, though it was unclear on whose orders he acted.
☝️
One point is worth recalling here. Within days of
the drone incident in Leipzig
, without any investigation or trial,
the German authorities were already declaring unequivocally that Russia was to blame and demanding the closure of
our Consulate General in Bonn
and
the Russian House in Berlin
.
Yet when it comes to the Hamburg trial, we are told that
all the circumstances must be thoroughly examined to establish a full picture of the crime
.
We shall see how the trial unfolds
, what conclusions it reaches and whether those who actually organised and oversaw the sabotage are publicly named and held to account.
👉
We are, of course, under no illusions.
Let me assure you that
Russia will continue to press for the truth
so that the Nord Stream case is not swept under the rug and those who masterminded and commissioned this major terrorist attack of our time do not, as the saying goes,
“get off the hook”
.

Original source: https://t.me/MFARussia/33351

✍️
Article by Ambassador of Russia to Indonesia
Sergei Tolchenov
,
“The grain initiative and the safety of shipping in the Black Sea”
, published in
The Jakarta Post
(November 11, 2026)
.
Key points:
• Food security demands an objective, comprehensive approach grounded in verifiable facts rather than political insinuations. Yet representatives of the EU continue to exploit this sensitive issue to stoke alarmist predictions of surging food prices and impending famine - while predictably laying the entire blame on the Russian Federation.
• Despite escalating Ukrainian attacks in the Black and Azov Seas, claims persist that Russia blocks Ukraine’s agricultural exports. These assertions ignore the context, terms and eventual collapse of the Black Sea Grain Initiative, while overlooking critical realities: Western noncompliance with reciprocal commitments, ongoing restrictions on Russian agricultural exports and Ukrainian drone strikes threatening civilian shipping.
• During the first operational year, 32.8 million tonnes of food products departed Ukrainian ports. Of that volume, approximately 70 percent - 26.3 million tonnes - went to high- and upper-middle-income economies, with EU member states absorbing 40 percent of all shipments. By contrast, African nations received just 4.1 million tonnes, including a meager 780,000 tonnes destined for sub-Saharan Africa.
• This pattern persisted in subsequent periods. The figures demonstrate that the actual distribution of Ukrainian exports diverged sharply from the humanitarian narrative presented to the international community. From the Western and Ukrainian standpoint, the corridor served commercial and logistical priorities rather than humanitarian ones: while agricultural cargo moved into European ports, the corresponding sea corridors provided cover for incoming military shipments to Kiev.
• Following Ukrainian attacks this past summer against oil tankers servicing the Caspian Pipeline Consortium, not a single public condemnation was issued by the EU. This double standard suggests that freedom of navigation and the protection of critical infrastructure are defended as matters of principle only when politically expedient.
• The operational data illustrates the reality at sea. Since the launch of the special military operation, Ukrainian forces have deployed 331 unmanned aerial vehicles, 40 unmanned surface vessels and two Neptune cruise missiles against commercial and civilian traffic in the Black and Azov Seas. These strikes killed 18 crew members - including foreign nationals - damaged 228 civilian vessels (96 foreign-flagged and 128 Russian-flagged, with dozens hit repeatedly) and sank four.
• For Indonesia, the core of this story remains clear: affordable staples, predictable logistics, unrestricted access to reliable global suppliers, including Russia. Food security must remain a shared objective
rather than an instrument of geopolitical leverage.

item.content:encoded:

✍️
Third Russia-Africa Summit: Building on Our Partnership
An article by Russian Ambassador to South Africa and Lesotho
Roman Ambarov,
published in
IOL
, The Lesotho Tribune and The Public Eye newspapers (12-13 November 2026)
🔴
Strong African participation
The Third Russia-Africa Summit and Economic and Humanitarian Forum
, held in Moscow on 27–29 October, brought together representatives
of 51 out of 54 African countries,
alongside business leaders and experts.
For many African participants, particularly first-time visitors, the summit offered an opportunity to
discover the “real Russia”
and form their own opinions beyond the narratives often presented in Western media.
🔴
Listening to Africa
For Russia,
listening to our African partners is just as important as presenting our own ideas.
The best results come when we identify shared interests and work out solutions together.
🔴
Equality and mutual respect
Russia and African countries are committed to developing relations based on sovereign equality, mutual respect and practical results.
🔴
Investment, not exploitation
Russian companies are encouraged to invest in African economies, establish local production facilities, share expertise, cooperate with local businesses and create jobs.
African countries should have greater opportunities to
process their own natural resources, expand industrial capacity and move beyond dependence on raw-material exports.
🔴
Important Agreements
and
a Roadmap until 2029
The Summit concluded with
a comprehensive 101-point Moscow declaration outlining
priorities for Russia-Africa cooperation across politics, security, economic development, humanitarian affairs, environmental protection and climate issues.
🔴
Addressing the legacy of colonialism
The Declaration supports developing legal mechanisms to assess and compensate for colonial-era damage inflicted on African countries, as well as the return of cultural property taken from the continent.
🔴
A practical roadmap for 2027
-2
029
The Russia-Africa Partnership Forum Action Plan provides a framework for implementing Summit agreements and advancing cooperation between high-level meetings.
🔴
Expanding trade and investment
Russia-Africa trade
exceeded US$27 billion
in 2025, with
significant potential for further growth and diversification
.
Around 85% of commercial transactions between Russia and African countries are conducted in
national currencies,
including the Russian rouble.
🔴
Energy and nuclear cooperation
Russia is ready to
strengthen cooperation in oil and gas, hydropower and nuclear energy
.
Rosatom signed three agreements with Togo, Rwanda and Uganda during the Summit, advancing potential nuclear energy projects.
🔴
Food security and agricultural development
Russia exported
over 18 million tonnes of grain
to Africa in 2025 and another
13 million tonnes
in the first nine months of 2026.
We will
continue
supplying grain, agricultural products and fertilisers.
🔴
Technological sovereignty
Russia is ready to
share its technological expertise and digital solutions with
African partners.
☝️
The objective is to help African countries develop their own technological capabilities, knowledge and skills, reducing dependence on external providers.
🔴
From commitments to implementation
The Summit established priorities and frameworks for expanding cooperation.
❗️
The next step is to
translate agreements into concrete projects and maintain regular engagement with African partners.

💬
Remarks
by Russia’s Deputy Foreign Minister Sergey Ryabkov to
RT
following the trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi
(November 12, 2026)
Key points
:
•
Unlike in previous rounds
, this time we focused largely on
the prospects for building a security architecture in Europe
and in the area surrounding the current conflict that would ensure that any future agreement holds.
•
It would be premature to speak of restoring trust between the parties.
That is not how we approach the issue. But judging by our discussions
yesterday
and
the day before
, I believe that, given the necessary political will,
we can build something workable and realistically achievable
while avoiding uncontrolled escalation.
•
We worked through the entire agenda in detail in
bilateral meetings between delegations
,
in smaller groups and in plenary sessions
. We used every tool at our disposal in the search for solutions. There should be no doubt about that.
•
We have made progress
.
That is indisputable
. In the past,
we have seen setbacks and reversals
. At times, agreements that seemed within reach were torpedoed.
👉
That is what we want to avoid.
• The presence of
General Grynkewich
, NATO’s Supreme Allied Commander Europe and a four-star general, brought
a considerable degree of professional expertise
to these discussions on their side.
•
Russia's military representatives
were there as well. They know the issues inside out. As far as we at the Foreign Ministry can judge,
they conducted themselves with exceptional professionalism
.
•
The Europeans, who insist on being part of this process, clearly feel sidelined
. They cannot come to terms with the approach we have consistently and firmly advocated and pursued. Clearly, they find it unacceptable.
•
The European countries are equally hostile to the ideas put forward by the US administration.
There is a very wide gap between their positions. Bringing the Europeans into the negotiations could therefore
undo the progress made
and derail efforts that have so far shown some promise and given us some grounds for optimism.
❗️
I hope those who previously sought to derail these efforts realise that the situation on the ground is shifting to Kiev’s disadvantage.

🎙
Comment
by Aide to the President of Russia Yury Ushakov following a meeting between Vladimir Putin, US President’s Special Envoy Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner
(November 12, 2026)
💬
Yury Ushakov
: Good evening, friends.
All of you are certainly aware that President of Russia
Vladimir Putin
received
US President’s Special Envoy
Steve Witkoff
and
Jared Kushner
today.
The conversation was very
substantive, constructive, frank and productive
– just like all their previous conversations.
At the outset of the meeting, the Russian President made
several important statements
in the presence of the press, setting the tone for the discussion that followed.
Notably, the American negotiators actively supported the
Russian President’s proposal
to apply the approach used in
the successful humanitarian operation in Aleshki
to another city beyond the line of contact, namely,
Konstantinovka
. <...>
👉
We are ready to begin demining operations immediately.
***
The President of Russia has once again supported the American side’s proposal to move towards resolving security issues for both Russia and Ukraine as part of efforts to shape
a future post-conflict system of European security
. <...>
The President recalled our vision of
the key pillars of the architecture of indivisible security
, which we presented back in 2021 in the form of
draft agreements with the United States and NATO on security guarantees
.
📄
These include
:
• the non-expansion of the NATO bloc,
• the non-deployment of threatening weapons systems near Russia’s borders,
• a return to the configuration of the alliance’s forces as it stood at the time the Russia-NATO Founding Act was signed.
To this list, which is not limited to the points I have outlined, we would like to add
certain new considerations
of our own, based on the lessons that we cannot – simply cannot – fail to draw from the present situation, in which the collective West has taken up arms against us, making no secret of its desire to save the Kiev regime and to inflict a strategic defeat on Russia.
For our part, the position of the Europeans has been comprehensively outlined. They are striving by every means possible to join the negotiations, but, as our President has said, they must decide
whether they want peace or the continuation of the war
.
☝️
So far, all their practical actions point precisely to the latter.
***
In the course of today’s negotiations, the behaviour of the head of the Kiev regime was also discussed – namely, the “friendly greetings” he publicly extends to the President of the United States.
It was also noted that in Kiev they do not want to end the war, because
they would immediately have to call general elections
, and no one wants to lose power.
Our President did not overlook the fact that the current American administration is working very insistently and persistently to achieve
a genuinely lasting settlement of the Ukrainian conflict
. <...>
Both we and the American side see great value in
the upcoming trilateral summit in Shenzhen
, which our Chinese hosts are organising.
During the talks, Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner gave a detailed account of their assessments of the trilateral contacts that
took place
in Abu Dhabi on November 10–11.
Both we and the Americans regard those discussions and contacts as
constructive and productive
. It was agreed that this negotiation process and this track of talks will continue.
In particular, support was expressed for an initiative discussed in Abu Dhabi to carry out
another prisoner exchange, which would likely be the largest to date
. The parameters of this exchange are currently being finalised.
***
Following these in-depth discussions at the Kremlin, the American negotiators have departed for Dublin, where they are due to meet with Zelensky and representatives of various European capitals.
We hope that the signals from Moscow
will be conveyed to them with the utmost care
.
